title: Editor shell and task hosting
purpose: All permitted editor users locate their current site, page, workspace and task. A task completes without unexpectedly leaving another draft.
evidence: S: competing left Panel Tab, Issues and AI modes; present dirty registry covers Settings/CMS. R: standalone shell and rail visible. P: single task arbiter.
problem: Independent modes can obscure each other; current discard guard can continue after failed discard. The same task needs a valid host in resource workspaces.
owner: Session owns navigation, not the document. module Workspace and active Task are independent; owner-specific drafts remain authoritative. IAF-20 adjudicates each action.
layout: Topbar: site identity + labelled Site settings; global History/notifications/Preview/eligible release. Rail: Add, Layers, Assets, CMS, Brand and Help utility. Bottom: Pages and status only. Inspector remains contextual. One active named task follows NAV-02; off-canvas AI opening requires explicit visible Editor target before execution.
panel: REDESIGN arbitration; KEEP approved placements. GEO-01. Resource task tray overlays body; Editor task replaces Inspector. Header contains task title, scope, close/back; body scrolls once; footer only when a task owns actions. Reject a permanent extra task column and automatic canvas navigation.
flow: Open named task → preserve origin → use or follow exact target → result → Close/Back restores frame. Replacing task runs its draft/operation guard. Unknown/denied request leaves current task intact. Nested comparison/picker owns a child frame. Direct rail navigation does not grow Back stack.
controls: Open/Close task: NAV-01/02, no content write/Undo. Site settings label remains discoverable at compact width. Command search uses exact same destination/capability as visible buttons; unavailable action explains why. Splitter: 16 px keyboard steps, bounds GEO-01, preference-only reset. Discard failure: “Could not discard this draft. Retry or stay”; never continue navigation.
states: Loading/failed task body uses existing error isolation; focus returns to invoking control. Hidden workspaces inert. Task drafts, cancelled navigation, unknown role and deleted target have distinct states. One foreground modal; no global shortcut mutates hidden canvas.
dependencies: IAF-02,05,14–22; existing Inspector integration contracts; navigation preference aliases and command registry.
preservation: Preserve all seven right-column modes including Inspector, old shortcuts, error boundaries and useful global dialogs. Migrate old panel IDs to canonical host; no page/schema rewrite.
tests: T-IAF01-1: CMS record draft → History → Close restores text/query/focus. -2: Issues replaces AI only after draft decision. -3: failed discard keeps origin. -4: denied target leaves prior task. -5: F6/Tab/Escape never enter inert canvas.
unknown: Actual redesigned shell not implemented; specimen tests validate only selected navigation and geometry. Full browser/assistive-technology and role combinations remain acceptance.

title: Canvas, selection and responsive editing
purpose: Designers compose the intended page at an explicit authored breakpoint; view adjustments must not create accidental responsive overrides.
evidence: S: Desktop base≥1024, Tablet 768–1023, Mobile<768; existing Wide 1920 preset. R: empty canvas/local View and zoom. Existing Inspector runtime evidence remains separate.
problem: View dimensions, authored breakpoint and available editor space can be conflated. Resize and style-copy integrity risks remain FI-01/02, not solved by toolbar relocation.
owner: Document owns element tree/style overrides. Session owns selection, pan/zoom, overlays and preview width. Page root and element scope remain distinct; Inspector FD-INS/BIC control semantics remain normative.
layout: Local toolbar above canvas: Undo/Redo; ancestry; Desktop/Tablet/Mobile; width; Zoom/Fit; View. Width input does not become a topbar site setting. Wide is a Desktop preview preset. Selection labels identify component boundary and hidden/inherited state.
panel: REGROUP local toolbar; KEEP canvas. GEO-01 44h, two rows at canvas-column<720, growing with text. Inspector overlay at≤1366 changes occlusion only. Desktop authoring preview proposed 1440, Tablet 768, Mobile 375, Wide 1920; preserve stored custom width. Reject auto-switching CSS breakpoints on panel opening.
flow: Select canvas/tree → synchronized selection → optionally enter text editing/nested target → edit valid scope → explicit commit/cancel → Undo bounded edit. Desktop base cascades down; Tablet overrides continue to Mobile unless overridden; reset removes only that layer. Changing width resolves actual breakpoint and labels it; Fit changes zoom only.
controls: Custom width integer 240–2560 px; strict parsing, blank draft stays blank, zero/fraction/out-of-range inline error; Enter applies, Escape cancels. Do not strip invalid characters into a different valid number. Zoom uses existing supported presets/manual bounds; Fit explicit, no history. Parent/breadcrumb navigation is session-only. Drag shows valid parent/index, rejects invalid nesting, Escape cancels before drop; Move menu/keyboard alternative uses same validator. Inline text has visible editing mode; Escape leaves without losing already committed segments. Multi-select mixed values follows FD-INS, never reports first value as shared.
states: Empty page vs loading vs unavailable page distinct. Hidden breakpoint elements remain reachable through Layers and explain current invisibility. Read-only/locked operations blocked at command layer. Selection deleted by remote change clears to valid parent/page. Resize cancel restores starting values; no partial multi-selection mutation.
dependencies: Layer synchronization; engine nesting rules; responsive/pseudo style serialization; text editors; component overrides; preview/export renderers.
preservation: Keep marquee, nested selection, precise targeting, rotation/resize, overlays, device frame, copy/paste, keyboard and context-menu operations. Preserve breakpoint/: state payloads on clone/paste and undo. No new breakpoint schema.
tests: T-IAF02-1: open/resize panels at 1440/1280/1024 without changing authored width or override layer. -2: width validation and Fit distinction. -3: nested/multi/hidden/text selection round trip. -4: invalid drop/cancel/keyboard Move parity. -5: responsive styles survive duplicate/save/reopen/export.
unknown: Current Resize/Clipboard bugs not fixed. Device performance and full mutation/output parity not rerun in this phase.

title: Layers / Navigator
purpose: Designers target nested or invisible elements, understand hierarchy and reorganize safely.
evidence: S: tree, search/display settings, context actions and cross-page move exist. P: coherent selection/return contract; mutation tests not run.
problem: Tree movement, hidden status and canvas targeting need identical semantics; moving across pages can break page-scoped resources.
owner: Tree/document owns order/nesting and element identity; expansion/search are session preferences. A lock limits mutation, not ability to inspect. Component definition/instance boundaries stay visible.
layout: Rail Layers → sticky title/search/display options → virtualized tree → contextual menu. Indent+disclosure+type/name+visibility/lock signals. No CMS/assets management in the tree.
panel: KEEP/REGROUP;284 default 260–360, one tree scroll. Tree indentation cannot consume action targets; truncate names with full accessible name/tooltip, horizontal navigation remains keyboard-accessible.
flow: Search → reveal ancestors → select exact ID → canvas reveals target if possible → rename/move/hide/lock → receipt or inline error. Cross-page move → destination page/parent → dependency validation → one transaction → destination selected, origin return available. Cancel leaves tree unchanged.
controls: Rename preserves empty stored custom name/type-label behavior from FD-INS; Enter/blur commits validated draft, Escape cancels. Visibility labels distinguish current-breakpoint hide from editor-only visibility. Move up/down/into/out and Move to page are keyboard alternatives to drag. Tree arrow keys navigate/expand; selection and expanded state independent. Multi actions preflight whole target set and show mixed state.
states: No elements, no search matches and failed tree load differ. Invalid parent/locked ancestor/page-scoped component boundary explains reason before move. Remote deleted/relocated node updates selection by ID, not row position.
dependencies: IAF-02/05/11; nesting, lock, page/component scope and history validators.
preservation: Keep all current context actions/display options/search, multi-selection and page move. Preserve ID s, bindings, responsive and interaction targets during reparent. Page-local master cannot be stranded invisibly.
tests: T-IAF03-1: hidden nested child selected from tree. -2: invalid nesting rejected via drag and menu. -3: keyboard reorder one Undo. -4: cross-page component reference preflight. -5: search/expansion preserved after resource return.
unknown: Large hierarchy/focus virtualization and movement persistence require actual implementation validation.

title: Add, quick insertion and generated blocks
purpose: Editors insert the right primitive, composed block or linked component at an explicit valid target.
evidence: S: Add sections, catalogues, generation and linked definitions are distinct. BIC existing 69 block contracts govern supported registry insertion. P: clarify task grouping and restricted generation dispatcher.
problem: Catalogue items can be mistaken for reusable user masters. Generated commands currently rewrite section anchors but can forward unrelated mutation families.
owner: Add owns insertion intent; document owns resulting nodes; Components owns saved masters. No inserted block automatically becomes a linked component. Generating a block is insertion, not a general AI editing run.
layout: Add local categories Elements / Blocks / Catalog components / Saved components. Search, favorites/recents retained. Saved components exposes Manage components; Templates opens page-layout workspace; Generate a block remains Add subview.
panel: REGROUP existing 284 panel; quick-add modal retains bounded layout and target. Generated result uses same panel with prompt/result/status/Stop/Undo. Reject an additional permanent Build workspace.
flow: Choose category/search → choose target parent/index → insert validated node/instance → select result → Inspector. Generate captures page/root/anchor → request → validate insertion-only commands → commit → show result/Undo. Stop/Back/unmount invalidates run and aborts pending result; committed insertion remains honestly reported.
controls: Category/search changes no content. Search returns named kind and insertion scope. Insert disabled with parent/role/capacity reason. Generated prompt uses existing endpoint limits, not invented unlimited context. Result may only create the supported insertion tree; reject mutation of existing elements, tokens, page settings, component registry or release. Stale anchor requires reselection; no active-page fallback. Undo bound to transaction; refusal after newer history retains result and explains recovery. Generate prompt Cmd/Ctrl+Enter starts generation only when idle and valid; plain Enter inserts a newline. Active generation disables starting another run. This is a CTRL-01 keyboard exception.
states: No results vs unavailable catalogue vs quota/provider failure; generating/stopping/cancelled/inserted distinct. Keyboard Enter inserts at declared target; drag alternative available. No success toast before engine receipt.
dependencies: BIC/FD-INS; nesting; component adoption; template page mode; IAF-12 quota and AI contracts.
preservation: Keep all registry types, valid contextual/quick-add/paste routes, supported advanced native data, recents/favorites. Engine-only commerce/variant authoring has explicit IAF-23 disposition, not silent removal.
tests: T-IAF04-1: each BIC insertion route retains supported payload. -2: generated out-of-scope token/page command rejected whole step. -3: Stop before commit inserts nothing; after commit reports insertion. -4: stale target no wrong-page insertion. -5: Add → Manage → Back restores query/target.
unknown: No production generation request was run; provider/context quality and execution remain unverified.

title: Pages and page settings
purpose: Editors switch/create/organize pages and change the intended page’s metadata without editing site defaults accidentally.
evidence: S: folders, bulk operations, filename/slug, page settings staged SEO/Social/Advanced. P: primary bottom Pages management and exact owner return.
problem: Page switch, rename and URL change have different consequences; page visibility must not imply unimplemented page-password protection.
owner: Page ID owns document/metadata; folder owns organization only. Site SEO defaults stay IAF-14. Existing permissions/capacity checked per operation; no role grant through bottom tabs.
layout: Bottom Pages switcher opens all-page list/management; active page named. Management has search, folders, Add page, bulk selection. Exact page action → Page settings with SEO/Social/Advanced and Done/Cancel. Page selection from any workspace intentionally enters Editor on selected page.
panel: REGROUP page access; work-area Pages sheet/default 560, max 720, bounded viewport−48; narrow full work area. Page settings dialog 720 max with sticky tabs/footer, one body scroll. Bottom remains Pages/status only; no canvas controls.
flow: Pages → exact page → switch after draft guards. Rename offers Keep URL / Update URL; URL change validates conflicts and redirect implications. Duplicate preserves subtree/styles/bindings with fresh node ID s and remapped internal refs. Delete prevents homepage/last-page removal, previews inbound links/templates/component scope; bulk validates all. Settings tab change retains same draft; Done awaits confirmed writer; failure retains input.
controls: Page name trim 1–100; folder 1–80; preserve canonical page schema validators. SEO title≤60, description≤160 on this writer; empty uses displayed fallback without copying it into storage. Slug uniqueness/route validation before commit. Visibility Live/Hidden; legacy password data displayed as unsupported/hidden, never newly promises protected output. Advanced head code remains existing permission/sanitization boundary. Reset field removes page override only where underlying model supports it.
states: Empty/search/permission/capacity states; saving/conflict/invalid slug; deleted page origin resolves containing list. Keyboard tab/arrow page navigation does not bypass unsaved guard. Existing multi operations one transaction with per-page outcome if backend differs.
dependencies: IAF-06 templates; CMS dynamic template filename/path; internal links; localization; shared component scopes; document save.
preservation: Keep folders, listings/structure modes, home/duplicate/delete/bulk/move, metadata and template routes. Renaming template filename must update or warn on dependent CMS path references; no silent broken dynamic pages.
tests: T-IAF05-1: metadata tabs retain unsaved input. -2: rename Keep URL versus Update URL. -3: delete home/last rejected. -4: duplicate retains responsive/native data. -5: CMS template page rename impact and resource → page switch explicit.
unknown: Backend role/capacity and broken-reference scans not exercised in empty demo; schema differences across other writers require integration tests.

title: Templates and page import
purpose: Editors start a new page or deliberately replace a named page with a reusable layout.
evidence: S: template workspace, preview, filters/plan gate, create/replace and backup-version path. New-page import catch can claim nothing changed after page creation.
problem: Insertion/replacement scope and backup failure need truthful outcomes; component packages must not be mistaken for page templates.
owner: Template catalogue owns source layout; application writes chosen/new page. Site design tokens apply through supported existing paths, not guaranteed magical conversion. Component identities are independent.
layout: Add → Templates or empty-page entry → template workspace with categories/search/cards and preview. Persistent header shows Create new page / Replace [page]. Premium/locked state names actual entitlement. Back preserves Add query or page origin.
panel: KEEP dedicated workspace; GEO-01 local nav/list. Template preview full work area with primary Apply, secondary Back, mode+target visible. Import dialog uses bounded 720 shape. No resource task UI behind active modal.
flow: Preview → choose create/replace → preflight dependencies/dirty state → for replacement create safety backup → apply → select resulting page. Backup failure offers Retry/Cancel or separately warned Replace without backup. Import failure reconciles whether page was created/partially changed; offer receipt-based recovery, not false “nothing changed”.
controls: Create page name follows IAF-05; target page required for Replace. Apply cannot double-submit; operation ID/revision binds response. Search/filter is view-only. Brand compatibility is a read-only summary: a tokenized template resolves current site Brand values; a fixed built-in template keeps its own styling. This design adds no Brand application toggle or shared-token mutation. HTML/template import keeps sanitization and supported native mappings; report unsupported portions.
states: Loading/empty/no match/plan restriction/provider failure; backup pending/failed; import partial/conflicted. Cancel before commit no page mutation; after commit Close returns result. Keyboard preview navigation/focus preserved.
dependencies: Pages, Brand, template parser, history backup, publication eligibility and component/pasted HTML boundary.
preservation: Keep catalogue categories, premium gating, preview and new-page/replace routes. Preserve prior page backup and original references until commit. Do not flatten linked components silently.
tests: T-IAF06-1: new page fails after creation reports actual state. -2: replace backup failure cannot silently continue. -3: role/target change before apply blocks stale commit. -4: Back returns exact filter. -5: imported supported styles round-trip.
unknown: Premium template retrieval and import mutation/runtime outputs not tested here.

title: CMS collections, records and dynamic pages
purpose: Content editors (site read; writes EDITOR+) manage schema and records; designers connect templates. Success means server-confirmed content, correct bindings and known publication eligibility.
evidence: S: four collection screens exist; only Records/Fields top tabs, others menu. Record save awaits mirror receipt; field update is fire-and-forget. Delete recovery creates new record ID. R: empty CMS navigation/collection actions visible only.
problem: Hidden dynamic/settings destinations weaken discovery; optimistic schema state can overstate persistence; fake Undo can break record references.
owner: Site collection/schema/record ID s are canonical; Inspector owns binding/presentation, never source content. Collection writes and document bindings are separate operations with separate receipts. Record Published flag means eligible for next site output, not a deployment.
layout: CMS workspace navigation: Collections list and Data. Collection header names collection and exposes Records / Fields / Dynamic pages / Collection settings as visible local tabs. Records table → record subview. Fields list → detail. Import CSV / Import JSON local collection actions; no extra global module.
panel: REGROUP existing workspace. GEO-01 nav 240/table flex/detail 320; record work area subview 720–960 with header Back/title/status and footer Save record/Cancel. Long record form one scroll; field inspector stays detail, becoming subview if<480 remains.
flow: Create/select collection → define fields → record → edit → Save record → pending → confirmed/failed/conflict. Preview draft fields is explicitly local; Preview saved record uses saved template data. Dynamic pages: choose non-home template path, slug pattern and SEO fields → validate → Save dynamic-page settings → eligible count. Template edit follows exact page with return. Collection delete preflights records/bindings/generated pages; do not unbind document before server result without compensating transaction.
controls: Field name/key separate; key lower case letter first then letters/digits/_/-, reserved/duplicate guards. Types text, number, rich text, image, boolean, reference, slug, textarea, date, multiselect; legacy types preserved. Required, text min/max, numeric constraints: unset≠0; invalid draft retained. Bound key/type/reference target locked with usage explanation. Dynamic slug uses {field-key}; report missing keys/template/duplicate URL s/empty results. Record published checkbox explicit next-publish meaning. CSV preview/mapping/partial result; JSON import cannot claim atomic server save. Recovery after delete labelled Restore as new record with new-ID/incoming-reference warning; exact undelete deferred pending backend support.
states: No collections, no records, no matching results and failed load differ. Saving locally/queued/confirmed/conflicted separate; failed form stays. Required/missing/deleted references visible; no replacement by first record. Schema mismatch disables incompatible bindings, retains saved raw reference for repair. Bulk operation report per record; no general mixed schema edit.
dependencies: IAF-08 bindings/data; Pages template filename; assets references; export/publish; CMS service tombstones and conflict handling.
preservation: Keep all existing field types, constraints, CSV/JSON imports, record preview and dynamic settings. Collection export is not established in the inspected UI; no new export interface is promised. IDs/references stay unchanged by navigation. Acknowledged schema writers and coordinated collection deletion are required fixes. Existing delete recovery remains available as explicitly Restore as new record.
tests: T-IAF07-1: failed/queued field save never Saved. -2: rename/delete bound field preflight. -3: draft preview vs saved vs deployment. -4: deleted record restore clearly new ID, incoming refs not falsely repaired. -5: dynamic URL collision/template rename. -6: partial CSV/JSON retry cannot duplicate confirmed records.
unknown: Authenticated service persistence, real data binding and dynamic-page output not runtime verified. Large tables/field migration acceptance still required.

title: Data sources, site variables and element conditions
purpose: Designers bind supported data and distinguish reusable strings from session providers and element visibility logic.
evidence: S: sources currently in-memory; site Variables in project settings; string condition operands are literal while resolver expects source Id objects; hidden marker has no established output consumer.
problem: Durable/live-source claims and apparently working conditions would mislead users. Schema, record content and presentation binding must stay distinct.
owner: CMS Data owns session Sources and site Variables. The selected element owns its bindings and conditions; Inspector Content is their canonical management home under BD-20. Static property ownership remains FD-INS: href/playback Behaviour, background Style. An adjacent Bind affordance opens the same property-specific binding editor and returns to that row. Device visibility remains Behaviour.
layout: CMS → Data → Sources / Site variables; a read-only Conditions index may list page/element and Locate. Locate enters the exact Inspector Content condition with an origin return frame. No second condition writer in the final IA. Preserve the current raw legacy entry/data until validated migration; after relocation the old entry redirects to the same Inspector owner. BD-20 P1–P4 expanded dynamic capability is approved direction with detailed contracts still proposed, not optional rejected scope.
panel: REGROUP existing CMS Data navigation; MOVE element condition editing to existing Inspector Content, not a separate expression workspace. Existing property rows keep their static tab owners; shared binding subview names property, record context and scope. New dynamic controls require the BD-20 detailed handoff before implementation; no untested control-density claim.
flow: Source → inspect/replace JSON → validate → session result. Variable → key/value → usage impact → commit document. Conditions index → exact page/element → Inspector Content → inspect legacy expression/unsupported status → edit only through the supported owner → return to originating index/field. Legacy route remains until lossless migration passes. Never promise working published visibility from the current no-op consumer. New property binding/condition/filter/sort output follows the separately approved BD-20 program.
controls: Variable key ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$, unique; empty string valid. Rename/delete previews known placeholders; unresolved export literals remain diagnostics. Source JSON errors retain draft; Refresh only with provider getData, otherwise Replace JSON. Preserve raw condition operators ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=, contains, startsWith, endsWith, exists, empty and AND/OR groups; legacy string operands remain literals, source objects retain sourceId. Unknown operators stay stored/unsupported. New typed semantics, coercion, migration and publication policy are not invented by this IA closure. Binding reset removes the reference, not a record.
states: Session source loss on reload is explicit. Invalid JSON/key, missing reference, mismatch, failed lookup and unsupported condition output differ. Preserve raw expression data and permission guards through relocation. Approved future authoring is labelled Planned; no simulated evaluator or automatic publication block is implied.
dependencies: BD-20 / CMS-DYNAMIC-BINDING-DESIGN.md owns the expanded dynamic-system detailed design. P1–P4 remain approved direction awaiting complete evaluator, serialization, migration, field compatibility and canvas/preview/publish contracts. P5 is conditional as recorded there. Durable external providers and a new publication-block policy require separate decisions. Current site variables retain document persistence.
preservation: Preserve source IDs, raw expressions and existing binding identities. Never reinterpret legacy strings as paths, silently remove a current authoring path before replacement, or keep two final writers. M07-100 future Behaviour/optional placement is superseded only by BD-20; device visibility remains Behaviour. CMS Sources/site variables stay distinct from Brand tokens.
tests: T-IAF08-1: session-source reload limitation. -2: legacy literals/source objects/operators round-trip unchanged. -3: deleted source/field repair retains references. -4: current unsupported output never appears verified. -5: variable rename shows usage. -6: Conditions index/old entry enters exact Inspector Content target with return and no duplicate writer. -7: Bind from a Behaviour/Style row returns to that row. -8: BD-20 expanded feature cannot ship without its separate detailed/output/migration acceptance.
unknown: Existing-product IA and expanded BD-20 destinations are settled. The BD-20 draft still has detailed semantics questions (published omission vs hidden, missing record-page destination, rich-text compatibility, draft record handling); its full dynamic feature is not DESIGN READY under FD-IA-09. Durable providers remain outside approved expansion.

title: Assets, fonts and image versions
purpose: Users find/manage their assets; site editors assign exact placements and manage site fonts without assuming workspace-wide asset sharing.
evidence: S: user-owned discovery, optional site association; page/CSS usage only; version creates new asset; grace delete separate from Composer Undo. R: Assets drawer and manager empty state captured; service mutations not tested.
problem: Zero known page placements is not globally unused; uploading/versioning, choosing and replacing all uses have distinct effects. Folders/font/library identity must not be broadened to team ownership casually.
owner: Asset owner user; write additionally requires site EDITOR when site-associated. Page/CMS field owns chosen source and local alt. Asset default alt differs from placement override. Site fonts are resources; applying font is Inspector/Brand.
layout: Rail Assets opens workspace: All/Recent/Used on this site/No known page placements/My folders/Fonts. Search+type/format/tag/folder/sort; grid/list+density; multi toolbar. Detail tabs metadata/known usage/versions. Contextual picker reuses library query but carries target/property and Choose/Cancel; no unrelated auto assignment. Preserve insertion separately: Assets manager offers Insert and return / Place on canvas. These deliberately return to Editor with a temporary left Asset picker replacing Add/Layers (284px, same bounds), keeping the canvas exposed. The picker names Insert image at [parent/index] or Replace [image/property]; selecting an image element does not silently decide replace versus create. Choose/Cancel and Back to library preserve origin/query. Drag starts only from this visible picker, uses canvas drop validation and cancels with Escape. OS file drop remains available directly on Editor canvas. Click/keyboard Choose uses the same captured valid target and transaction as drag.
panel: REGROUP/KEEP management workspace GEO-01; detail 320. Image editor dedicated work area subview with own preview/controls; below 1280 controls stack, no tiny inspector. Picker 720 dialog; large selection uses full work area while preserving captured target.
flow: Upload → progress → confirmed asset → optional Choose target. Edit image → preview → Save version → new asset receipt → optional Replace on chosen pages. Existing placements unchanged until explicit replacement. Replace across site previews known page placements/version family, chosen pages and unknown CMS/other-site usage; atomic document transaction proposed. Delete asset uses grace recovery; folder delete has separate consequence, no fake global Undo. Selected replacement policy: preflight the entire captured page-placement set, then apply all document replacements in one transaction/Undo unit. Any invalid target prevents the batch; there is no partial-success claim for this new transaction. Asset upload/version history is a separate receipt and cannot be rolled back by that document Undo. The current per-source partial implementation must change to meet this contract. If the original placement target disappears or becomes locked, retain the chosen asset and require a new target; never mutate the current arbitrary selection. Upload confirmation and placement confirmation are separate. Completing insertion restores the prior Add/Layers panel and selects the inserted element; replacement retains original selection. Cancel returns to the previous workspace/picker and does not delete completed uploads.
controls: Crop Free/1:1/4:3/3:2/16:9; rotation/flip/zoom; brightness/contrast/saturation−100..100; blur 0..20 px. Resize positive integer≤8192, empty follows crop,0 invalid, aspect lock. Export Web P/JPEG/PNG, default Web P quality 85 (10–100); PNG quality applicability explained. Save version separate asset upload and history receipt; history failure does not erase successful file. Search indicates partial/truncated server result; reset filters view only. Choose revalidates target/resource access; alt field distinguishes default vs override. Fonts upload/add never implies applied typography.
states: No assets/no results/failed list/truncated list; upload pending/failed/cancelled; duplicate/version conflict; missing/deleted asset fallback. In flight upload deletion immediate versus post upload grace explicitly different. Permission/retry/recovery visible. Bulk selection stable ID s across pagination.
dependencies: IAF-07CMS src fields; FD-INS media; Brand fonts; ingestion limits; usage scanner coverage; asset GC/grace server jobs.
preservation: Keep stock/icons/font management, filters/sorting/metadata, folders, paste URL, image editor, clone/version/replace/delete/recovery. Keep ID s/version relationships; no new workspace asset sharing. Fix FI-03 independently. Preserve used assets even when partial scanner reports 0.
tests: T-IAF09-1: picker return exact image/record field after workspace visit. -2: Save version preserves existing placements. -3: replacement all-or-none with one Undo; failed preflight changes no placements. -4: search failed≠empty. -5: grace Undo vs folder/in flight delete. -6: CMS usage not declared absent by page-only scan. -7: management → Place on canvas → keyboard/drag create or replace → exact return; invalid drop/cancel and OS file drop retain supported behavior.
unknown: Actual upload/quota/provider/image-output/GC and cross-site privacy not exercised. All numeric image controls source-located, not newly tested.

title: Brand and shared website design resources
purpose: Designers manage site tokens/type styles and apply them with known shared reach; chrome design tokens remain an entirely separate system.
evidence: S:14 token kinds, shared Composer history, duplicated style catalogues, inert preset binding, class apply depends selection, JSON import fidelity limits. R: Brand workspace navigation and token groups observed.
problem: Brand definitions, catalogues and local class application lack one clear task model; importing/previewing may imply unsupported fidelity or hidden global changes.
owner: Site project.settings.designTokens owns tokens/aliases/type styles; Composer history and document save. Inspector applies references/local overrides. Preview Light/Dark is session; Dark mode Off/Auto is saved. Component masters remain IAF-11.
layout: Brand local nav: Tokens (Colours, Typography, Spacing, Other named kinds), Reusable styles (Type styles/presets, Classes), Tools (Dark mode, Checks, Starters, Import/export). Other kinds explicitly lists radius, shadow, motion, border, opacity, z-index, breakpoint, grid, sizing, icon, imagery. Header Undo/Redo, Review changes, Restore points. Catalogue component styles becomes Browse sections in Add link, never master management.
panel: REGROUP workspace; GEO-01 nav 240/detail 320, preview flex; token detail replaces body if insufficient space. Colour scale/logo URL/connect-to-token bounded subtasks, exact return. Reject wider Inspector and duplicated style editors.
flow: Open exact token from Inspector → usage/scope → edit compatible value → live applied → document pending/saved → Back exact element. Delete used token → replacement compatible choice → usage impact → one transaction. Starters now Preview → Confirm → one Undo with restore point. Import → validate → mapping/impact → apply → receipt; export names fidelity. Before starter commit capture a local token/document checkpoint usable by document Undo. When a server restore point is available, create it before commit. If unavailable/offline/standalone, retain the existing local starter capability: show “Local recovery only; no server restore point” and allow explicit Apply with local Undo, or Cancel. A failed local checkpoint blocks application. Never claim a queued server restore point is confirmed.
controls: Token edit uses existing kind validators; invalid values remain local draft, no silent seed reset. Alias must same compatible kind; cycles/deleted targets blocked. Seed reset and delete separate. Classes Apply shows named selection; absent target choose Editor target, no hidden selection. Dark Auto creates missing dark aliases only after restore point; existing preserved. JSON array or {schemaVersion, tokens}; Update matching retains absent, Keep existing skips matches; show added/modified/skipped/type+spacing unsupported new/alias literalization. CSS/JSON/Tailwind exports distinct; Tailwind dark-mode loss explicit. CSS strategy media/data attribute/off export-only, not site Dark mode.
states: Loading/migration read-only/invalid tokens/usage unknown/empty type distinct. Used token delete blocks when usage unknown with Retry. No generic Save button for live applied edits. Restore point retrieval server confirmed, restoring one document Undo unit, conflict check; cannot claim external CMS/media restore.
dependencies: Inspector resolved values; font assets; shared history; export token closure; starter application; migration gates.

title: Saving, offline state, conflicts and recovery
purpose: Editors know what is safely stored and recover without overwriting newer work or unrelated resources.
evidence: S: local recovery banner Keep changes dismisses only; conflict Reload latest/Save backup/Overwrite, Brand format conflict blocks Overwrite; document import scope bounded. Existing FI-04 collaboration recovery risk.
problem: Queued/local/synchronized/published are different; save completion cannot claim edits made after captured revision. Closing conflict is not resolution.
owner: Document revision owned Composer+site persistence; CMS/asset/component/site-setting writes separate. Draft registry tracks applied/unapplied/job state. Save receipt must name captured revision/hash and server revision.
layout: Bottom status only: Unsaved /Saving revision… /Saved at… /Offline—local changes /Conflict /Save failed. Click opens status details with owners/jobs/retry. Recovery notice own actions; conflict foreground modal; saved history recovery IAF-18.
panel: REGROUP status+recovery; bounded 720 conflict form grow with diff; no extra always-on panel. Notification alone insufficient for blocking conflict; stable banner/status entry remains.
flow: Edit → local applied → queue captured revision → serverack → mark that revision only. Newer edits remain pending. Offline queue as actually supported, otherwise explicit local only. Recovery offer preview/backup → Keep changes(local dismiss)or Reload latest guard → reconcile. Conflict Reload latest/Save backup/Overwrite as eligible; Overwrite CAS recheck and impact, not blanket remote-reset. Closing dialog keeps conflict status. Backup failure must not discard local recovery or trigger reload. Separate Download backup from an explicit Continue to reload: successful generation/download initiation is labelled “Download started”, not proof that a file was retained. On serialization/download-initiation failure retain conflict, local recovery and draft; offer Retry/Cancel. Reload requires deliberate confirmation and current-revision checks. This corrects the source-only risk in ConflictModal and AquibraStudio, whose current finally path can reload after backup failure.
controls: Save/retry idempotent per captured operation; no formatting-time out Saved guess. Discard draft not Undo already applied shared operations. Backup download/generated receipt distinct server sync. Overwrite unavailable Brand format conflict. Restore check current revision and dependencies; after new work offer new copy/merge/review only if implemented, otherwise Save backup+Reload rather than fake automatic merge.
states: Loading/local dirty/saving/confirmed/failed/offline/queued/conflicted/recovered/permission lost; partial multi owner receipt shows which saved. UI status live announcement polite except blocking error; focus retained on retry.
dependencies: Every writer, collaboration CAS, history checkpoints, provider jobs; FI-03/04 and IA-X integrity risks.
preservation: Keep autosave/manual save/local recovery/backup/conflict actions and bounded history. No assumption document Undo reverses server CMS/media/master operations. Authoritative value not duplicated in shell state.
tests: T-IAF22-1: edit during save leaves new revision dirty. -2: queued≠server Saved. -3: conflict close unresolved. -4: Brand format Overwrite blocked. -5: restore after remote edit no false Undo. -6: multi owner partial save Retry only unfinished. -7: Keep changes≠synchronized.
